script: Lock my funds because of your mistake? Have your bank's social media ruined. For some reason, god knows why, I thought I'd trust a very small and local credit union with some of my money. I had that whole "small town vibe" feel, like it was safer than the big banks. I was like, "Yeah, I am all about that community support." But here's the thing… The ATM was glitching, and my card just wouldn't pull cash. I walked into the branch, asked the clerk for help, and he slid me a code that'd let me grab cash straight from my account. "No special treatment, just a standard feature," he said, like I'd be the first to need it. I thought I was done. Until… The system flagged my account for review—apparently a tiny accounting error meant my balance hadn't been deducted on time. I didn't even go overdraft; I was just a victim of their glitch. Now my money was locked for over a month, and every time I called the support line, the reps were snarky, throwing shade about my "foreign sounding last name." I couldn't even get a straight answer. I was losing sleep, feeling like a joke, and my stress level was through the roof. But wait — it gets worse. My cousin from back home, who's always into some hack, suggested a Russian service that pays people a few rubles (like 1 USD cent each) to post whatever you ask them on social media. It sounded insane, but I was desperate. I dropped $3 of my life's savings, crunched some AI prompts, and hit the website. The service let me pick a profile that looked American or something else. I set up a campaign to flood the credit union's social media with complaints. (I know, right?) I felt like a hacker in a movie, but this was real. And the plan was in motion. Within hours, their Facebook, Instagram, and even their own website were plastered with "I am locked, my money's gone!" "Worst bank ever!" "Support is a joke!" The manager of the call center, who had been shouting at me for a week, finally picked up. He called me, said, "We get it, we're sorry, and if you don't want your account anymore, we'll transfer your balance plus $50 to any other bank." I could almost feel the relief like a wave washing over me, like I was finally getting a win. He offered a full transfer and a $50 bump.
